_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy P1, November 2024 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Mathematical
Literacy questions hang off shared scenario boxes: the scenario (tables, graphs, plans and maps
described in bracketed words) is the 'context' of the first sub-question of each block and applies
to the sub-questions after it. memo_answer gives the guideline's working and final answer with
decimal commas kept; the guideline's mark codes (M method, A accuracy, CA consistent accuracy, RT
reading from table, C conclusion, O opinion, S simplification, R rounding) and level tags are left out.

questions.context: 2.2 Mr Paul is a businessman. He wants to attend a meeting and searched for a meter taxi online. He found the prices of two companies: Daniel's company and Jerry's company. Daniel's company charges the following for a single trip: • a minimum call-out fee of R50 per trip and the first three kilometres are free; • thereafter, R12,00 for each additional kilometre or part thereof. Jerry's company charges a flat rate of R14,50 per kilometre.
questions.text: Write down the formula for calculating the cost for Daniel’s company in the form of: Cost =
questions.topic: Finance: tariffs, VAT, UIF and exchange rates
questions.memo_answer: Cost = R50 + R12,00 x (number of km travelled - 3)

questions.text: The distance for a single trip to the meeting is 80 km. Mr Paul makes the statement that Jerry’s taxi company will be the cheapest. Verify, showing ALL calculations, that his statement is correct.
questions.topic: Finance: tariffs, VAT, UIF and exchange rates
questions.memo_answer:
Daniel: R50,00 + R12,00 x (80 km - 3) = R50,00 + R12,00 x 77 = R50,00 + R924,00 = R974,00
Jerry: R14,50 x 80 = R1 160,00
His statement is incorrect (Daniel's company is cheaper).
questions.memo_note: The guideline writes Jerry's working as 'R14,00 x R80,00'; the rate is R14,50 per km and the answer R1 160,00 uses it.

questions.text: Mr Paul had another trip. He paid Daniel R1 214 for a single trip. Determine the distance travelled during this trip.
questions.topic: Finance: tariffs, VAT, UIF and exchange rates

questions.text: Mr Mnotho and his wife both secured new jobs overseas. They applied at a Boys High School for their two sons. The first son will be doing Grade 10 and the second son will be doing Grade 8. They will be staying at the hostel. Mr Mnotho received the following information regarding the school fees. [TABLE 3: SCHOOL FEE STRUCTURE FOR 2024: school fees R48 800,00; hostel fees R66 800,00; total R115 600,00.] School fees must be paid before the end of January. Hostel fees must be paid at the beginning of each year. Discount for siblings is offered as follows: • second child gets 10% discount on school fees and 5% discount on hostel fees; • third child gets 15% discount on school fees and 10% discount on hostel fees. Calculate the total discount amount that Mr Mnotho and his wife will get from the school.
questions.topic: Finance: financial documents, income and expenditure
questions.memo_answer:
Discount on school fees = R48 800,00 x 10/100 = R4 880,00
Discount on hostel fees = R66 800 x 5/100 = R3 340,00
Total discount = R4 880,00 + R3 340,00 = R8 220,00
